Indigenous Health Assessment (Adult 15–54 Years)

Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:
  • Acute diarrhea x 3 days (4–5 watery/loose stools/day) with mild abdominal pain and one episode of vomiting.  
  • Possible low-grade fever (patient unsure).  
  • No blood or mucus in stool.  
  • Hydration adequate; able to drink fluids; no signs of dehydration on video review.

- Relevant family medical history:
  • Father: hypertension; died of bowel cancer at age 62.  
  • Other family history: Not recorded.

- Medications (including OTC or shared medications):
  • “Lexapro” inhaler (yellow) for asthma – dose/route/frequency not documented (name uncertain; clinician unfamiliar).  
  • No current antidiarrheal or other medications.  
  • OTC products: none reported.

- Immunisation status reviewed: Not recorded.

- Sexual and reproductive health: Not recorded.

Investigations (as indicated)

- Fasting BGL and lipids (or random BGL if needed): Not ordered.
- Cervical screening (if eligible and due): Not applicable/not discussed.
- STI screen (urine or swab – chlamydia/gonorrhoea if age 15–35): Not discussed.
- Mammogram (if eligible): Not discussed.
- Other pathology (e.g., HbA1c, iron studies, Vitamin D): Not ordered.
- Stool culture: To be considered if diarrhea persists ≥7 days or blood present.

Management Plan

- Education on acute diarrhea care:
  • Maintain adequate oral hydration; add oral rehydration solution (e.g., Dioralyte).  
  • “Soft diet” advised: crackers, toast, mashed/boiled vegetables; avoid dairy (except yogurt), meat, eggs, and fish until 48 hours symptom-free.  
  • Introduce yogurt for probiotic benefit.

- Red-flag advice:
  • Seek review if ≥6–8 diarrheal episodes/day, signs of dehydration, blood in stool, or symptoms persist >1 week.  
  • Stool sample and possible antibiotics if blood present or symptoms prolonged.

- Follow-up:
  • Re-contact service or present to hospital if red-flag symptoms occur.
  • Routine follow-up not scheduled at this consult.

Quality checks

● Missing but clinically expected elements: BP, pulse, temperature, weight/BMI, waist circumference, immunization review, smoking/alcohol/substance history, physical activity assessment, mood screening, basic vision/hearing checks, urinalysis, preventive screening discussions (e.g., cervical/colorectal), medication verification (exact inhaler name/dose).  
● Internal contradictions: Father described as “had hypertension/has hypertension” yet noted deceased (conflict noted).  
● Transcript quality: Clear overall; minor inaudible sections (medication name uncertain: “Lexapro/Laxepro”).
